he:Shabbat/Musaf for Shabbat:6.en: Returning the Torah to the Ark

he:Shabbat/Musaf for Shabbat:29.en: Remember us for life, O King who desires life, and write us in the book of life – for Your sake, O God of life.

he:Shabbat/Musaf for Shabbat:34.en: He makes the wind blow and the rain fall.

he:Shabbat/Musaf for Shabbat:36.en: Who is like You, compassionate Father, who remembers His creatures in compassion, for life.

he:Shabbat/Musaf for Shabbat:62.en: You formed Your world long ago, completing Your work on the seventh day. You loved us and chose us, elevating us above all languages, sanctifying us with Your commandments, drawing us near to Your service, and calling Your great and holy name upon us. You gave us, O LORD our God, in love, Sabbaths for rest and New Moons for atonement. But since we sinned before You, our city was destroyed, our Temple desolate, our glory exiled, and our honor taken from our lives. We cannot perform our duties in Your chosen house, the great and holy house called by Your name, because of the hand stretched out against Your Sanctuary. May it be Your will, O LORD our God and God of our fathers, to bring us up in joy to our land and plant us in our borders, where we will perform our obligatory offerings before You: the daily offerings in their order and the additional offerings according to their law. And the additional offering of this Sabbath and this New Moon, we will perform and offer before You in love, as You commanded us in Your Torah through Moses Your servant, from Your glorious mouth, as it is said:

he:Shabbat/Musaf for Shabbat:139.en: The Levites used to say in the Temple on the Sabbath:

parts.text: I will sing sweet psalms and I will weave songs,
to You for whom my soul longs.
My soul yearns for the shelter of Your hand,
that all Your mystic secrets I might understand.
Whenever I speak of Your glory above,
my heart is yearning for Your love.
So Your glories I will proclaim,
and in songs of love give honor to Your name.
I will tell of Your glory though I have not seen You,
though I have not known You.
By the hand of Your prophets,
You gave a glimpse of Your wondrous majesty.
Recounting Your grandeur and Your glory,
of Your great deeds they told the story.
They represented You in many visions;
through them all You are One without divisions.
Aged on the day of judgment,
yet on the day of war,
a young warrior with mighty hands they saw.
Triumph like a helmet He wore on his head;
His right hand and holy arm to victory have led.
His curls are filled with dew drops of light,
His locks with fragments of the night.
My diadem of beauty He shall be.
His head is like pure beaten gold;
His people have adorned Him with a crown.
is the dwelling place of right;
may He prize it as His highest delight.
Like a crown in His hand may His treasured people be,
a turban of beauty and of majesty.

with a crown He adorned them.
They were precious in His sight,

my glory is on Him.
He is near to me when I call to Him.
He showed the tefillin-knot to Moses,
when the LORD’s likeness was before his eyes.

the humble He does raise –
He glories in them;
He sits enthroned upon their praise.

is true:
O seek the people who seek You.

My many songs please take and hear
and may my hymn of joy to You come near.
May my praise be a crown for Your head,
May a poor man’s song be precious in Your eyes,
To the One who sustains all,

to me Your head incline:
accepting it as spice,

May my prayer be to You sweet song.
For You my soul will always long.

en:Shabbat/Musaf for Shabbat:98.en: Bow, take three steps back, as if taking leave of the Divine Presence, then bow, first left, then right, then center, while saying:

parts.text:
It was taught in the Academy of Elijah: Whoever studies [Torah] laws every day
is assured that he will be destined for the World to Come,
“The ways of the world are His” – read not,
Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Ḥanina: The disciples of the sages increase peace in the world,
“And all your children shall be taught of the <small>LORD</small>,
and great shall be the peace of your children [
“your builders.” Those who love Your Torah have great peace;
there is no stumbling block for them. May there be peace within your ramparts,
prosperity in your palaces. For the sake of my brothers and friends,
“Peace be within you.” For the sake of the House of the <small>LORD</small> our God,
I will seek your good. ▸May the <small>LORD</small> grant strength to His people;
may the <small>LORD</small> bless His people with peace.

Instruction mentions 'In winter' and 'In Israel in summer' but does not specify the exact condition for the default text or the alternative. The text 'He makes the wind blow and the rain fall' is for winter (mashivHaruach) in diaspora, and 'He causes the dew to fall' is for summer (moridHatal) in Israel. The siddur text is ambiguous about the default condition for the first phrase.
